title: $\mathsf{EFI}\Leftrightarrow\mathsf{1PRS}$
abstract: A series of recent works has established EFI pairs as the "minimal" assumption for quantum cryptography. Recently, Cavalar et al. [CCC+26] showed that EFI pairs are equivalent to non-uniform expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS), and obtained a non-uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. We remove the non-uniformity in their construction and prove that EFI pairs are equivalent to expanding 1PRS. As a corollary, we obtain the first uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. Together with the equivalence of statistically verifiable one-way state generators and commitments proved by Batra and Jain [BJ24], this gives a quantum analogue of the classical equivalence between one-way functions, commitments, and pseudorandom generators.
summary: This paper proves a fundamental equivalence in quantum cryptography, showing that EFI pairs are mathematically equivalent to expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS). By removing non-uniformity from previous work, the authors provide the first uniform characterization of this relationship. This result establishes a deep quantum analogue to classical cryptographic theorems linking one-way functions and pseudorandomness.
main_problem: To prove the uniform equivalence between Efficiently Formed Information (EFI) pairs and expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS).
main_result: The authors establish the first uniform meta-complexity characterization showing that EFI pairs exist if and only if expanding 1PRS exist, providing a quantum analogue to classical cryptographic equivalences.
method: The proof adapts the random-start technique and uses entropy chain rules to remove non-uniformity from prior constructions, relating the existence of quantum states to computational hardness assumptions.
model_or_system: The analysis is conducted using quantum states (pure states) within the framework of quantum cryptography primitives like EFI pairs and 1PRS.
key_observables: Von Neumann entropy, algorithmic entropy, trace distance, and the entropy surplus.
important_parameters: Security parameter $\lambda$, output/key lengths ($n, r$), and the stretch factor.
main_assumptions: The proof builds upon prior results regarding non-uniform equivalence and relies on the random-start idea holding for quantum side information.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the equivalence relationships between EFI, statistically verifiable one-way state generators (svOWSG), quantum commitments, and 1PRS.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the equivalence ($	ext{EFI} \Leftrightarrow 	ext{1PRS}$) using advanced entropy analysis, culminating in a theorem that provides the uniform meta-complexity characterization.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the rigorous mathematical tools developed for bounding quantum entropy and proving computational indistinguishability are foundational to understanding the limits of quantum information processing.
